govdocs-archive_org-manual-of-zen-buddhi: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki’s Manual of Zen Buddhism gathers the essential Zen texts — sutras, koans, and commentaries. The great interpreter’s pages opened Zen to the West. Generations learned Zen from these pages. The Heart Sutra shines here. The book remains the classic Zen introduction.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-BurgessDonaldPS: Donald P. Burgess’s FBI inventory — Room 2, 113 14th Street NE, April 17, 1968 — lists seized items. The declassified inventory is a primary source. Inventories documented every search. Researchers value such files. The file belongs to the government archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-ClineRayS_Cline: This item — Book Reviews Including Ray S. Cline, creator unknown — is a set of book reviews. The file belongs to the intelligence archive. Cline was a CIA deputy director. Reviews shaped the agency’s image. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FBISolutiontoJF: This FBI memorandum — Assassination of President John F. Kennedy — is a Bureau file. The declassified memo is a primary source. The Bureau’s paper trail is vast. The memo may hold a clue. Researchers value such files. The file belongs to the assassination archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-LeikindSeymourS: This news article — ‘Instructor’s Apology Halts Charge,’ Seymour — is a press clipping. The apology ended the case. The charge was dropped. Clippings preserve the moment. The file belongs to the press archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-MaloneWilliamSc: William Scott Malone’s The Secret Life of Jack Ruby is a New Times piece. Ruby’s life was a Dallas mystery. The piece is gripping. Ruby shot Oswald. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-MartinezSotoJor: This FBI report of Special Agent James J. O’Connor, Miami — April — is a Bureau file. The declassified report is a primary source. The Miami office watched the exiles. Researchers value such files. The file belongs to the government archive.
myths-and-legends-of-our-own-land-volume: California and the Pacific slope contribute gold-rush ghosts, Spanish mission legends, and tales of the old Southwest in this volume. Skinner captures the romance of the newest-settled region, where yesterday's news was already becoming legend. A vivid scrapbook of Western coastal folklore.
the-head-of-kay-s: Wodehouse's early school novel follows the boys of Kay's house through cricket, rivalry, and schoolboy honor. Before Jeeves, the young Wodehouse was already a master of the school story. Funny, brisk, and full of the high spirits of Edwardian boyhood.
pictures-every-child-should-know-a-selec: Mary Schell Hoke Bacon introduces young readers to the world's great paintings — Raphael, Rembrandt, and the masters — with stories about each picture. Designed to cultivate taste and wonder, it brought art into American homes. A charming introduction to the gallery of civilization.
tales-of-st-austin-s: Wodehouse's St. Austin's stories capture school life — sports, friendships, and scrapes — with humor and affection. These early tales show the master's inimitable style taking shape. Essential for Wodehouse completists and school-story lovers everywhere. Even here, the future master of comedy is unmistakably present.
